topic-graphs: In graph theory, what is a vertex?
A vertex is a dot. The lines joining dots are edges.
What does an Euler circuit do?
Uses every edge exactly once and returns to the start
An Euler circuit uses every edge once. Visiting every vertex once is a Hamiltonian circuit.
A connected graph has an Euler circuit when...
Every vertex has an even degree
Exactly one vertex has an odd degree
Every vertex has an odd degree
It has no more than five edges
If every vertex has an even degree, you can always leave a vertex after arriving at it. Try it in the tool above.
topic-statistics: The sum is 25 and there are 5 scores, so 25 / 5 = 5.
The mode is the value that appears most often. 4 appears twice.
Which measure tells you how spread out the data is?
Mean, median and mode describe the center. Range and standard deviation describe the spread.
topic-finance: You borrow ₱10,000 at 10% simple interest per year for 1 year. How much interest do you pay?
10% of ₱10,000 is ₱1,000. The total paid back is ₱11,000.
In a cost-benefit analysis, a project is worth doing when...
The cost is as large as possible
The total benefits are at least the total costs
Compare what the project costs with what it gives back. If benefits are at least the costs, it pays for itself.
The loan amount and term stay the same, but the interest rate goes up. What happens to the monthly payment?
A higher rate means more interest, so each payment is larger. Change the rate in the calculator to see it.
topic-geometry: What is the straight-line (Euclidean) distance from (0, 0) to (3, 4)?
By the Pythagorean theorem, the distance is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.
What is the city-block (taxicab) distance from (1, 1) to (4, 5)?
Add the horizontal and vertical moves: 3 + 4 = 7.
Which statement is true on a flat grid?
Taxicab distance is never longer than Euclidean distance
Taxicab distance is at least as long as Euclidean distance
Moving only along the grid can never beat the straight line, so taxicab distance is at least as long.
topic-modern: With a Caesar shift of 3, what does CAT become?
C → F, A → D, T → W. Each letter moves 3 places forward.
How do you decrypt a Caesar message made with shift 3?
Decrypting undoes the key, so shift each letter back by the same amount.
Why is the Caesar cipher easy to break?
It uses very large prime numbers
There are only 25 possible keys to try
An attacker can try all 25 shifts in seconds. Modern security relies on much harder math.
